cases.scenario: Circular person nodes appear one by one and connector strokes extend between them.
cases.reason: Designed nodes and paths change count, opacity, and path length to explain relationships.

cases.scenario: A static relationship chart remains on screen while the editor cuts to a close-up.
cases.reason: The chart itself does not change over time.

cases.scenario: A map marker appears, a route draws, and a region changes color.
cases.reason: Map graphics are designed layers with time-based state changes; relevance is a separate question.

cases.scenario: The camera slowly zooms into an unmodified map image.
cases.reason: Only the camera transform changes; the graphic system does not.

cases.scenario: A yellow mask sweeps across one exact sentence in a document and an annotation enters.
cases.reason: The document may be static source material, while the animated mask and annotation are motion graphics.

cases.scenario: A PDF page is held for five seconds with no animated annotation.
cases.reason: No designed property changes over time.

cases.scenario: Real footage cuts between three camera angles.
cases.reason: Shot selection and cutting are editing, not motion graphics.

cases.scenario: A name label tracks a moving person and a line remains attached to the subject.
cases.reason: The footage is not motion graphics; the tracked label and connector are.

cases.scenario: A lower third fades from 0 to 100 percent opacity and slides into place.
cases.reason: It qualifies technically, although design quality may be low.

cases.scenario: A headline assembles word by word, then one term changes weight and color on the spoken emphasis.
cases.reason: Kinetic typography changes content, opacity, weight, and color over time.

cases.scenario: A photograph receives a slow pan and zoom with no added animated graphic layer.
cases.reason: Image movement alone is not sufficient for the pipeline's motion-graphics classification.

cases.scenario: Bars grow from zero to exact values while labels count up and settle.
cases.reason: Designed data marks and labels change to communicate quantities.

cases.scenario: A photorealistic 3D character reenacts an incident without labels or explanatory graphics.
cases.reason: It is animation, but not automatically motion graphics.

cases.scenario: Abstract 3D blocks represent institutions, rearrange by responsibility, and connect with animated lines.
cases.reason: 3D is being used as a designed information system.

cases.scenario: A designed shape expands into a full-screen mask and becomes the next scene's document frame.
cases.reason: The graphic transformation creates a semantic transition.

cases.scenario: Two shots are joined only by a dissolve.
cases.reason: A dissolve alone is an editing transition.

cases.scenario: A multi-layer designed collage has foreground, middle, and background cards while a virtual camera moves through the information space.
cases.reason: Camera animation participates in an authored graphic composition rather than merely moving over one photo.

cases.scenario: Sparse sampled frames differ, but continuous playback has not been checked.
cases.reason: Contact-sheet differences locate candidates but cannot establish the actual animated layer or transition.
